newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli unlinked bonds end higher.
newsitem.headline: Israeli unlinked bonds end higher.

text.p: Israeli bonds on Wednesday closed higher across the board led by a rise in unlinked bonds, traders said.
Indices:
* Government bonds general: +0.01 to 170.13
* CPI-linked government bonds: +0.03 pct to 171.14
* Dollar-linked government bonds: +0.31 pct to 166.77
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon - issued for four years): +0.12 pct to 169.94.
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.04 pct to 160.59
Volume was moderate at 161 million shekels.
"Unlinked bonds continued to rise today as investors believe that in the long run the Bank of Israel will have to lower the interest rate," said Amir Eayal at Epsilon Securities.
"The market predicts that the interest rate will go down. There are simply no sellers and unlinked bonds continue to rise despite falling yields," said Yossi Levi at Ahrayut Investment Management.
"Makams (which are also unlinked) offer high profits because inflation is expected to fall sharply in the next few months," Eayal said.
Traders said bonds linked to the consumer price index (CPI) were stable with most of the series closing almost unchanged.
"Most of the activity in inflation-linked bonds was concentrated in the (variable interest) Kfir which offers a slightly higher yield," Levi said.
"Dollar-linked bonds rose following the dollar's rise against the shekel on Tuesday," Levi added.
Traders noted that the market was indifferent to the government's announcement that it will seek further budget cuts.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the Treasury would propose an additional two billion shekels in 1997 budget cuts by early December.

The additional spending reductions will come on top of 4.9 billion shekels in cuts the government has already submitted to parliament. The supplementary cuts will now be incorporated into the original budget package.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
($1=3.23 shekels)
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211
